To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed a low jitter frequency quadrupler that is suitable as a low power, low jitter, fast frequency reference for a PLL in a high performance, low power SoC.

a new active inductance based XO with 192MHz output and 168fs jitter is presented, which is then used as the input for a quadrupler that achieves 96MHz output with 184fs jitter, which is the lowest jitter reported for any quadrupler to our knowledge, and the circuit occupies 0.04mm^2.
we have demonstrated a low jitter 192 MHz quadrupler that can serve as a low jitter reference for PLLs and MDLLs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
low jitter frequency quadruplers.
the design of a low jitter 192 MHz quadrupler in 28 nm CMOS technology.
the design and optimization of low jitter frequency synthesizer architectures, and their application to low jitter PLL, MDLL, frequency quadrupler and frequency divider designs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have designed a low power, low jitter, small area frequency quadrupler in 28nm FD-SOI CMOS that is suitable for use in a variety of low power applications.
this is the first quadrupler with a sub-picosecond jitter.
this work presents the first reference quadrupler with low jitter, and that it is the first to demonstrate the use of active inductor for a 48MHz XO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is a low jitter, low power, low area, fast, and robust reference quadrupler.
the 192MHz quadruple is the fastest, smallest and lowest power quadrupler with low jitter.
we have developed a low phase noise and low jitter 192 MHz quadrupler that can be used as an on-chip reference for a low power and low phase noise PLL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quadrupler is a viable alternative to a PLL or MDLL for fast, low power, low jitter reference generation.
a fast reference quadrupler can be used to reduce the power and area of a low jitter PLL, and can be used in place of a reference PLL in many cases.

a quadrupled crystal reference with sub-picosecond jitter can be achieved using only a few transistors and passive components, and that it can be used as a low power, low jitter, fast lock PLL reference.
